thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-sre — latency SLO breach detected on us-east-1 streaming cluster. p95 up 2.6s -> 4.9s, p99 climbing. Auto-escalation to page.

oncall-sre: I’m on it. grabbing graphs now. can someone post which model/route is spiking?

ryan: seeing it on /v1/stream-chat (redwood-medium). throughput normal but tail latency spikes and a few streaming stalls.

mira: adding context — started ~07:12 UTC, small ramp then sustained tail at p99. Some requests show chunked streaming stall > 12s before next token. :eyes:

eng-runtime: noted. are we seeing increased KV cache misses or long kernel times?

ryan: KV miss rate up ~3x. degraded node showing repeating ECC correctable errors in syslogs.

infra-hw: we’re seeing ECC events on accelerator-23 (node: eu-accel-23). thermal readings spiked before the first ECC. could be thermal throttle causing long recompute/DRAM access latencies.

oncall-sre: immediate actions: 1) route new streaming traffic away from eu-accel-23 2) enable fallback routing to cpu-backed replica for slow streams 3) drain in-flight sessions on node. Executing now.

eng-runtime: routing change applied: `route-policy set stream prefer=eu-accel-pool healthy=true fallback=cpu-fallback-oct` — confirmed partial failover. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: action taken by @oncall-sre: routing update, node marked draining. Link: https://console.redwood.internal/incidents/9801234567

mira: customers impacted? any tenant throttles showing? cs team pinged.

customer-success: flagged two enterprise tenants with increased 5xx due to streaming stalls, opened tickets and notified account owners. No public outage yet but degraded UX on long responses.

ryan: collecting traces — attaching snippet of the streaming stall stack (truncated):

```
2026-03-15T07:13:02Z - stream:send_chunk duration=12.4s node=eu-accel-23 kernel=matmul_q8
GPU ECC: correctable error count=42
thermal: gpu_temp=92C fan=95%
```

eng-runtime: that matches a thermal-induced clock throttling window. When GPU throttles, memory ops stall and KV cache lookups block, stacking latency.

infra-hw: healthcheck logs show fan pwm oscillation around 92C -> spike then drop -> spike loop. Possible fan controller firmware bug or degraded fan bearing.

oncall-sre: plan: 1) immediate live mitigation = keep node drained, scale up spare capacity in us-east and eu (temporary) 2) enable more aggressive streaming timeouts to avoid long stalls 3) schedule hardware replacement for eu-accel-23 4) run firmware patch on similar nodes after triage.

ryan: rolling out timeout change: `streaming.timeout_token_gap=6s` as a temporary mitigation. This will close long stalls and surface faster fallbacks.

mira: rolling capacity: provisioning +4 instances in eu and +2 in us-east dedicated pool. ETA for extra nodes ~6m.

eng-runtime: also enabling prefix/KV caching bypass for the affected model to reduce KV pressure on accel nodes while capacity ramps.

incident-bot: autoscale triggered +6 instances in dedicated pool — check: https://console.redwood.internal/infra/autoscale/9801234567

customer-success: customer-facing note proposed: "We are investigating elevated latency on streaming responses; mitigation in progress, no data loss. We'll follow up with timeline." Approve?

oncall-sre: approve. send now and add link to support tickets.

infra-hw: hardware triage: recommend replacing fan and running memtest on eu-accel-23. ECC count per hour indicates progressive deterioration. Will coordinate with datacenter.

eng-runtime: post-mitigation checks: p95 back down to 1.2s after full routing failover and extra capacity. p99 still elevated but trending down. Streaming stall incidents dropped by ~88%.

mira: putting summary for postmortem: root cause likely thermal/fan oscillation on eu-accel-23 causing transient ECC correctables and GPU frequency throttling -> increased kernel latencies -> KV cache pressure -> streaming stalls and SLO breaches.

ryan: saved key logs and traces to /incidents/9801234567/traces.tar.gz

oncall-sre: final ops note: node eu-accel-23 quarantined and set offline. hardware replacement ticket #HW-4522 created. Follow-up: schedule firmware update for fan controllers @infra-hw and run rolling memtest for similar GPUs in the pool.

customer-success: updated customers with mitigation and ETA for fix. CS will follow up after hardware swap.

eng-runtime: postmortem action items: 1) add automated fan/frequency oscillation alert 2) add quicker fallback to cpu-backed streaming for nodes with ECC spikes 3) tune streaming timeouts per model profile.

oncall-sre: closing the page. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. excellent cross-team coordination. :thumbsup:
